title: Adaptive kernel prober and head packing for heterogeneous MQA/GQA quirks (Llama/Mistral/Qwen)
author: Keisha Nguyen
release_notes: Improves model-specific kernel selection and head-packing behavior to reduce tail latency and token cost for heterogeneous MQA/GQA workloads. No API changes. Rollout guarded by feature flag and per-customer opt-in.
description: Motivation: We continue to see fragmented performance across Llama/Mistral/Qwen variants under mixed MQA/GQA workloads. Small microbursts and mismatched per-head packing produce higher tail latency and underutilized kernels on A100/RTX-class nodes. This PR introduces two runtime mechanisms: 1) a light-weight kernel prober that runs a micro-benchmark at model load (and on fallback events) to detect best-fit kernel variants for the observed head/hidden shape and quantization profile, and 2) a head-packing scheduler that groups heads into stable execution clusters at dispatch time, reducing kernel churn for heterogenous multi-head setups. Approach summary: - Kernel prober: a non-blocking, timed probe that iterates candidate kernel paths (planar/interleaved/packed) at very low token-counts and records normalized latency for the current hardware and sequence distribution. Probe runs under the same process but at low priority; results are cached in the model profile and exposed to routing heuristics. - Head-packing scheduler: groups attention heads by tiling affinity and memory stride compatibility. Packing decisions are guided by a cost heuristic that factors per-head dimension, quantization grain (4/8-bit), and recent sequence-length histogram. The scheduler also emits safepoints for the continuous-batching layer to avoid oscillation-induced small-batch regressions. - KV-window compactor hint: when packing identifies highly skewed head groups we emit a compact hint to the KV manager to tighten the eviction window, reducing memory pressure on long-lived conversational sessions. Checklist: - [x] kernel prober implementation (C++ runtime + protobuf model profile fields) - [x] head-packer scheduler (Rust lane allocator module) - [x] continuous-batching safepoint integration - [x] unit + integration perf tests - [x] docs and runtime flags (runtime.flags.kernel_prober, runtime.flags.head_packing) Commits summary: - Add kernel prober and profile schema (runtime/kernel_prober.cpp, proto/model_profile.proto) - Introduce HeadPacker and packing heuristics (scheduler/head_packer.rs) - Continuous batching safepoint hooks and tests (batch/continuous_safepoints.rs) - KV hint plumbing and tests (kv/compact_hint.go) - Docs and feature flags (docs/perf/head-packing.md, configs/runtime_flags.yaml) High-level changed areas: - runtime/ (kernel prober, profile caching) - scheduler/ (head packing, lane allocator integration) - batch/ (continuous batching safepoints) - kv/ (compact hint API) - proto/ and configs/ (profile schema + flags) - tests/perf/ (benchmark harness and regression checks) Review conversation (high level): - Ravi: "Great direction. Two concerns: probes running on hot nodes could bias tail latencies; can we ensure the prober yields and limits retries?" - Author: "Prober runs at niceness 19 and uses a token budget; added jitter and single-shot fallback after initial sampling. See runtime/kernel_prober.cpp:ProbeRunner::run()." - Lars: "The head packing heuristic looks promising, but we need a fallback for models with dynamic heads (custom attention)." - Author: "Added safe opt-out via model profile flag and an explicit per-request header to bypass packing for experimental models." - Sofia: "KV compactor hints may interact poorly with long-lived sessions; please add a conservative default and telemetry before enabling broadly." - Author: "Set default hint aggressiveness to 0.2 (conservative) and added telemetry counters: kv.compact_hint_emitted, kv.compact_hint_applied." CI/Checks: - CI initially failed: tests/perf/head_packing_regression.py flaky on AMD runner (timeout). - Flake fixed by extending timeout and making test runner use local CPU affinity; CI rerun passed. Merge notes: - Merged via squash on 2024-04-22 after perf benches on canary cluster showed median latency improvement of 8-12% and 18% reduction in small-batch tail (95p) on mixed MQA/GQA traces. - Rollout plan: feature flag off for all tenants; enable on canary tenants for 2 weeks, monitor metrics (latency p50/p95, kernel-churn, kv.evictions). Monitoring dashboards: perf/head_packing_canary, kv/compact_hints. Known limitations and follow-ups: - Prober currently measures on representative low-token sequences; for extremely long context patterns it may prefer kernels that are suboptimal at 32k sequence lengths. Follow-up task ENG-4472 to add sequence-length stratified probing. - Head-packer conservative defaults may miss micro-optimizations on homogenous models; follow-up ENG-4499 to add model-category specific profiles.
